# laight

This package contains a growing collection of miscellaneous functions that I 
have found useful for day-to-day tasks in medical statistics/biostatistics.

## Installation

You can install the development version of `laight` by running the following:

``` r
remotes::install_github("jaklaight/laight")
```

## Examples

```{r}
library(laight)
```

`shades()` produces a ggplot object, with partitioning of a probability density 
curve using alpha (the "shades") and additionally provides probabilities at 
stated cut points.

```{r}
shades()
```

`flagpoles()` produces a ggplot object with a similar idea to shades. This plot
is also a probability density curve and provides a "flagpole" that points in 
either direction and provides probabilities of being above or below where the 
flagpole is planted.

```{r}
flagpoles()
```

`ordinal_bars()` produces a ggplot object and is useful for plotting counts such 
as adverse events in clinical trials, where the counts also have associated levels 
of intensity (e.g. severity) or some other ordinal quality. `ordinal_bars()` 
plots counts of given categoriesand shows the ordinal scale, with option to
split by group (e.g. treatment).

```{r}
set.seed(1)
data <-
  data.frame(
    category = rep(c(rep("Burn", 5), rep("Nausea", 5), rep("Headache", 5),
                rep("Pain", 5), rep("Other", 5)), 2),
    ordinal = as.factor(rep(c(1,2,3,4,5), 10)),
    count = c(rpois(25, 1), rpois(25, 1.5)),
    group = c(rep("Control", 25), rep("Intervention", 25))
    )

ordinal_bars(data, category, ordinal, count, group, sort = "descending")
```

`recruitment_plot()` produces a ggplot object which displays counts at each
time point, cumulative counts, and projected counts. Useful for inspecting how
recruitment is going in a clinical trial. Optimistic example provided (i.e. 
actual recruitment exceeds projected recruitment).

```{r}
set.seed(1)
data <-
  data.frame(
    time = seq(as.Date("2024-10-01"), as.Date("2026-09-01"), by = "month"),
    recruited = rpois(24, 3),
    projected = cumsum(rep(2, 24))
  )
data$time <- factor(format(data$time, "%b %Y"), levels = format(data$time, "%b %Y"))
recruitment_plot(data, time, recruited, projected)
```

`variable_search()` allows searching for variables across a list or environment 
of data.frames.

```{r}

my_list <- list(iris = iris, mtcars = mtcars)
variable_search(my_list, c("sepal", "T"))

```
